gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states, in each maker's own words, which low-profile switch family every number-pad board's sockets accept and which trims are soldered; I could not confirm those maker statements either, because every maker store returned HTTP 429 today.
standout_why: I compared against the two rival pages that opened, purchase.fyi and keebscout.com (both in ChatGPT's results, neither cited). Between them they already carry most of the mechanism: keebscout says 'a low-profile socket takes low-profile switches only' and 'Pick the board first, because the board picks your switch family for you', and that K5 Max hot-swap is 'on higher trims'; purchase.fyi says the K3 Max/K5 Max sockets are 'compatible with Gateron LP and NuPhy LP switches', that NuPhy's V3 'uses incompatible Nano sockets', and that Bluetooth on most low-profile boards polls at 90 to 125 Hz against 1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz. What they lack is a per-board statement for the number-pad candidates (Lofree Flow Lite 2 100, NuPhy Air100 V3, Logitech) and any maker wording. The three RTINGS pages returned only navigation and Technobezz returned HTTP 403, so the cited pages were not compared; the score could be 0 if RTINGS already states socket compatibility.
decides: It does not change the pick. No candidate fails on mechanism; the finding only confirms that the shopper should choose the board for the switch it ships with, because a low-profile socket locks them into one switch family, and should check the Keychron K5 Max listing says RGB hot-swappable if they want to change switches (GamePadSquire: white-backlight versions are not hot-swappable). This angle should not lead the page unless the maker wording in 'unsourced' is read from the makers' pages once the stores stop rate-limiting.
